notes:
Space can search video speech, captions, translations, chapters and keyframe images by meaning using a local Semantic search package on Apple Silicon, with text search as a fallback when semantic retrieval is unavailable.
Search results show matched frames, explain whether words or meaning matched, and preview the original source moment before opening the timeline. Duplicate passages merge, loosely related results fold away, and thumbnails load in batches.
Semantic indexing covers all BaoCut projects and unfiled videos by default. Exclude projects or individual videos, re-index items, move or rebuild the index on another disk, and add external video/image folders as read-only Space sources. External folders require an explicit re-scan to pick up changes.
Index status combines speech and visual progress with remaining-time estimates, pauses for thermal throttling and optionally battery power, and exposes per-item coverage. Visuals are enabled by default after the package is installed.
Text embedding can use the Apple Silicon GPU with CPU fallback; visual embedding uses the CPU. Switching compatible text and multimodal bundles preserves text vectors. Earlier experimental semantic indexes re-encode once for the new encoder identity.
Agents can search the video library by default in conversations without a project, narrow searches by requested exclusions, and use index-status, related-video, relevant-passage, retake, glossary and frame-matching tools. Library questions search Space before supplementing from the web.
Writing tools use relevant passages and retain the searched topic when handed to an agent. Saved Markdown citations open the cited video moment. Semantic assistance also supports related videos, translation reuse, glossary checks and retake candidates.
Chapter candidates use windowed topic-depth scoring and reuse current indexed chunks, with visual shifts as supporting evidence. Chapter guidance accounts for recordings longer than an hour.
Agents are instructed to save a video brief after transcription and finish with a task summary. Briefs stay with the editable video through undo and package transfer; video details offer an expandable brief with time links and copy support.
Local Fish Audio S2 Pro adds built-in voices and transcript-backed voice cloning with seeded generation and cancellation. Packed 8-bit weights and staged codec loading reduce memory use; the model is restricted to research/non-commercial use.
Antigravity CLI joins the agent providers with streamed sessions, images, model switching and interruption. It requires agy 1.1.15 or later and Full access; automatic temporary BaoCut MCP configuration and live Google-account validation remain unavailable.
Import timed single-transcript ElevenLabs Scribe JSON without running inference, preserving word times and speaker IDs. No-space token boundaries survive captions, transcript display, search and text exports; older imported documents need re-import to gain those flags.
Model downloads support several named mirrors for model repositories and tools, source selection by group, clear per-part failure details, completion of missing parts and reuse of shared components already installed.
Timeline scrubber previews and pointer-position seeking are restored, and captions/filmstrips follow scrolling correctly. The add-chapter-at-playhead action is removed; existing chapter rename, removal and boundary editing remain available.
Image previews add arrow/Home/End navigation, smoother switching and a bottom thumbnail strip that clears annotations and macOS window controls.
Read-only search and Q&A turns stay out of background tasks and their running badge. Download cards become video cards after landing, new video cards open the split editor, inactive video tabs show useful previews, and dismissed legacy-import result banners stay dismissed.
Semantic match thresholds remain uncalibrated. Semantic models currently support macOS Apple Silicon; Windows retains lexical search. Web index management is read-only. Search moment previews play original source footage without timeline overlays.
macOS packages are signed and notarized. Windows CPU, CUDA and Vulkan packages are unsigned and require the Microsoft Visual C++ v14 x64 Redistributable. Real GPU/model inference, UI/export and paid agent calls are outside the automated release checks.
